name: Natural Theology

objectives.text: Identify things God made, such as the sky, sun, animals, and trees, that show he is powerful and wise
Name general revelation as God making himself known to everyone through the things he has made
Retell how Psalm 19 describes the heavens speaking of God without words to every land
Describe how God's gifts of rain, seasons, and food show his goodness to all people
Explain that God also makes himself known through the conscience he has written on every human heart
Distinguish general revelation from special revelation by comparing the two halves of Psalm 19
Identify ways God points Job to creation to display wisdom and power far beyond human understanding
Explain that creation shows God's eternal power and divine nature but does not reveal how sinners are saved
Explain from Romans 1 how people suppress the truth about God they know from creation and are therefore without excuse
Analyze how Paul uses what his pagan hearers knew from creation and providence in his speeches at Lystra and Athens
Analyze the limits of general revelation by identifying truths it cannot reveal, such as the Trinity, the incarnation, and the atonement
Explain how the order and intelligibility of the universe reflect the eternal Word through whom all things were made and are sustained
Explain Calvin's teaching on the sense of the divine in every person and on Scripture as spectacles that bring creation's witness into focus
Explain the Reformed understanding of reason as a servant of revelation that works under the authority of Scripture
Explain how the Westminster Standards describe what the light of nature teaches about God, worship, and moral duty and why it leaves people accountable
Compare Thomas Aquinas's view of what reason can know about God apart from Scripture with the Reformed emphasis on the effects of sin on the mind
Evaluate the twentieth-century debate between Karl Barth and Emil Brunner over whether there is a natural knowledge of God
Compare how classical and presuppositional apologists within the Reformed tradition assess the use of natural theology
Write an essay arguing from Scripture and the Reformed confessions why special revelation is necessary to complete what general revelation shows

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies: creation showing God's power, naming general revelation, Psalm 19, Romans 1 suppression and no excuse, nature not revealing salvation, limits of natural theology, Logos and order, reason and revelation, and the capstone essay on special revelation. Folded the sunset versus Bible comparison into a Psalm 19 lesson that distinguishes general and special revelation. Dropped 'observe God's power in a storm' because it duplicates the kindergarten objective, and dropped 'apply the truth that no one has an excuse' because it is now covered by the Romans 1 objective. Removed the Paley overview and the Darwinism and design objective because the design argument belongs to the sibling sub-topic Arguments for God's Existence. Merged 'defend faith and reason' into the reason and revelation objective. Added objectives on providential goodness (Acts 14, Matthew 5), conscience (Romans 2), Job 38, Paul at Lystra and Athens, Calvin's sense of the divine and spectacles of Scripture, the Westminster light of nature, Aquinas compared with the noetic effects of sin, the Barth and Brunner debate, and classical versus presuppositional assessments. Anchored the objectives to Belgic Confession 2, Westminster Confession of Faith 1.1, 1.6, 1.10, 10.4, and 21.1, Westminster Larger Catechism Q2, and Canons of Dort 3/4.4, and replaced whole-chapter references with specific verse ranges.
